A contributor's tooling is their choice, and the repository neither assumes it nor requires it. Config for a harness is an installable pack, never a tracked root; a gate may verify a harness that is CLAIMED, never demand that one be present. The test is that a clone with no agent tooling installed is green. Measured costs of not holding this, all from 2026-08-07/08: control-plane-check.py exits 1 on a tree with no .claude/, so a bare clone is red on arrival for anyone who simply has not installed the harness; the content pin on .design/tooling/control-plane.md digests the WHOLE of .claude/settings.json, so wiring a second tool drifts an upstream design doc even though control-plane-check.py exits 0 on both sides; and because actions/checkout builds the PR merge commit, that drift is imposed on every branch based against a fork's main, including branches whose whole purpose is to be cherry-picked upstream, where none of the layer may travel. Proposed in RFC-15 section 7.

```day-telos
{"witnesses":["gate-result"]}
```
